subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
passage: Playgroup note, Tuesday. Sabina held out a block that had stuck halfway in its hole and looked up at Nirmala, Sabina's mother. Nirmala gave it a slight turn, and Sabina pushed it home, then clapped. Later Sabina brought the next block over in the same way. I told Nirmala that asking was a fine first step and a small turn is something Sabina might try alone. The playgroup helper

qa.q: What did Sabina do after the block stuck halfway in its hole?
qa.a: Sabina held out the block and looked up at Nirmala.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling when clapping at the end?
qa.a: Sabina was pleased and proud, having pushed the block home after the slight turn. 😊

qa.q: What could Sabina try before handing over the block, and why?
qa.a: Sabina could give the block a small turn alone before handing it over, because the turn is what got it to fit.

qa.q: How does Nirmala see being handed the block?
qa.a: Nirmala is asked for one small turn and sees it succeed at once, so she is likely glad to help and pleased to see Sabina finish it.

grounding: A toddler hands a stuck block to the mother, who turns it slightly before the toddler pushes it in.

subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
passage: On the wooden floor of their Kottayam home, Jomon pushed a triangle at the triangle hole, but it caught on one edge. He tried twice, then turned and held it up to his amma. His eyes stayed on her face. She turned it a little in her fingers and set it back on the hole. Jomon pushed, and it dropped. He clapped both hands and laughed out loud.

qa.q: What was Jomon feeling when he clapped and laughed?
qa.a: He was delighted and proud that he pushed the block in himself after Amma's small turn.

qa.q: What else could Amma try next time to help him learn?
qa.a: She could turn it slowly while he watches, so he sees the move she made and can try it himself.

qa.q: How does the moment feel for Amma?
qa.a: She gets to help without taking over, and enjoys seeing him finish it and laugh.

grounding: A toddler hands a stuck block to his mother, she turns it slightly, and he pushes it the rest of the way, then claps.

subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
passage: Zanele's big brother Yosef was watching cartoons in the Durban flat when Zanele toddled past with a stuck circle block. She had tried the hole three times. Now she held it up to Mama and looked at her, waiting. Mama tilted it, just slightly, and gave it back. Zanele pressed it in with one finger. It fell with a thunk. She clapped hard, and Yosef clapped too.

qa.q: How can you tell Zanele felt proud?
qa.a: She clapped hard after pressing the block in herself.

qa.q: What small step helped here, and why?
qa.a: Mama tilted the block only slightly and gave it back, so Zanele could finish the job herself.

qa.q: How might Yosef see his little sister's success?
qa.a: He seems happy for her and joins in, clapping too.

grounding: A toddler hands her mother a stuck block, her mother tilts it slightly, and the toddler pushes it in and claps.
